governing_specs.FBD-100342: User Claims Specification V3.00 (KeyCloak/AD, realm Translink, operator-react-client / CloudFareWeb) — para indices are docx paragraph numbers
governing_specs.FBD-100363: Translink Ticket Editor Specification V1.00 — para indices are clean-extract paragraph numbers
governing_specs.FBD-100306: Merit Web Specification V3.00 — closest governing spec for the Administration/Merit editors (NOT in the named grounding set)
governing_specs.FBD-100383: TFTS Operator Hierarchy v4.00 — PDF, NOT machine-readable with current tooling; hierarchy facts cited from FBD-100342 instead
governing_specs.FBD-100266: Device Heartbeat Functionality & Reporting V3.00 — Alerts / Comms Monitor only; does not cover the Settings sub-pages in this batch

action_vocabulary.REWRITE: Behaviour grounded in a named spec; title/preface/steps corrected for conformance.
action_vocabulary.REGROUND: A label / role / screen / surface was wrong or drifted; corrected against spec.
action_vocabulary.SPLIT: Case bundles more than one behaviour/action; recommend splitting (grounded).
action_vocabulary.GAP: Feature/label not present in any provided spec; marked GAP, do not assert.
action_vocabulary.UNCONFIRMED: Plausible and/or specified outside the named grounding set; access role grounded where possible, behaviour not verified against provided specs.

meta.no_invention_note: Every asserted role, screen, label and field below traces to a cited paragraph. Where a detail is absent it is left as an explicit GAP/UNCONFIRMED marker per CLAUDE.md — never filled.

cases.title: Access — portal tasks match the operator's assigned claims
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that the functions available in the ABT Operator Portal are limited to the claims assigned to the signed-in user's KeyCloak user group.
preconds: GIVEN two operators exist in the Translink realm, each assigned to a different KeyCloak user group whose composite claims differ (e.g. one with AdminFullAccess, one with AdminReadAccess / report-only)
AND the ABT Operator Portal (operator-react-client) sign-on page is displayed

steps.when: each operator signs on with their Active Directory credentials
then: each operator sees only the portal functions granted by their group's composite claims
functions not granted by their claims are not available to them

cases.change_note: Regrounded terminology: the system has no free-form 'user roles' — access is by composite claims assigned to KeyCloak user groups, which users inherit (para 129-132). Renamed from 'Access rights differ by user role'. Sign-on is via AD credentials (para 125).

cases.title: Sign On — valid credentials reach the ABT Operator Portal
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an operator with claims assigned can sign on to the ABT Operator Portal with valid Active Directory credentials.
preconds: GIVEN the ABT Operator Portal (operator-react-client) sign-on page is displayed
AND the operator has been assigned to a KeyCloak user group so that they hold at least one claim (a first-time user with no claims cannot access the portal)

steps.when: the operator signs on with valid Active Directory credentials
then: the operator is signed in
the portal landing page is displayed

cases.change_note: Split from 'Operator sign-on and navigation'. The original bundled sign-on plus 'each menu option opens its page' (a compound multi-predicate THEN). Sign-on is the behaviour under test here; a separate menu-navigation case (or per-module claim case, see 4102857) should own menu coverage. Regrounded portal name to 'ABT Operator Portal (operator-react-client)'.
gaps: **GAP** — the exact set of menu options and which page each opens is not enumerated in FBD-100342 — confirm on the live portal before writing a navigation case

cases.title: Sign On — operator can sign off the ABT Operator Portal
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an operator can sign off the ABT Operator Portal and the session ends.
preconds: GIVEN an operator is signed into the ABT Operator Portal (operator-react-client)

steps.when: the operator signs off
then: the session ends
the sign-on page is shown

cases.change_note: Standardised title/preface. Portal named per spec. Sign-off mechanics themselves are not detailed in FBD-100342 but the portal existence and identity are grounded.

cases.title: Sign On — valid credentials reach the CloudFare Dashboard
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user with claims assigned can sign on to CloudFare with valid credentials and reach the Dashboard.
preconds: GIVEN the CloudFare (CloudFareWeb) sign-on page is displayed
AND the user has been assigned to the relevant user group (hosted: an Active Directory / ADFS group; SaaS: a KeyCloak group) — a first-time user with no claims cannot access the site
AND the user holds the Dashboard claim

steps.when: the user signs on with valid Active Directory credentials
then: the user is signed in
the Dashboard is displayed

cases.change_note: Regrounded 'username and password' to Active Directory credentials: hosted CloudFare authenticates via ADFS + AD (para 203); SaaS via KeyCloak (para 214). Dashboard is a real CloudFare claim (para 191). CloudFare web client is 'CloudFareWeb' (para 279).

cases.title: Sign On — Google account sign-on (UNVERIFIED)
cases.preface: This test is to confirm sign-on via a Google account. NOTE: no Google/OAuth sign-on path is described in the governing claims spec.
preconds: GIVEN the CloudFare sign-on page is displayed

steps.when: the user attempts to sign on with a Google account
then: **GAP** — outcome undefined: Google/OAuth sign-on is not in requirements

cases.change_note: FBD-100342 specifies authentication exclusively via Active Directory/ADFS (hosted) or KeyCloak fed from Active Directory (SaaS) — paras 203, 214-215. There is NO Google/OAuth identity provider in the spec. This case asserts an authentication mechanism that is not in requirements.
gaps: **GAP** — 'Sign on with a Google account' is not in FBD-100342 (AD/ADFS/KeyCloak only). Either Google federation was added to KeyCloak (needs a CR reference to become UNCONFIRMED) or the case is invalid. Confirm with the engineer before running or retaining.

cases.title: Sign On — user can sign off CloudFare
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a signed-in CloudFare user can sign off and the session ends.
preconds: GIVEN a user is signed into CloudFare (CloudFareWeb)

steps.when: the user signs off using the sign-off control
then: the session ends
the sign-on page is shown

cases.change_note: Standardised. Removed the specific 'back button' sign-off variant to a gap — not described in the spec.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — 'sign off via the browser back button' behaviour is not described in FBD-100342; verify on the live system before asserting it ends the session.

cases.title: Passenger Portal — sign on to an anonymous account
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a customer can sign on to the Passenger Web Portal with a card that has journeys in the previous seven days.
preconds: GIVEN the Passenger Web Portal sign-on page is displayed
AND the customer's payment card or mobile wallet has completed journeys in the previous seven days

steps.when: the customer enters valid card details
then: the customer is signed on to their anonymous account
the account home screen is displayed

cases.change_note: Passenger Web Portal is a customer-facing surface. No Passenger Web Portal specification is present among the named governing specs or in the requirement library search (found no 'Passenger Web / Passenger Portal / Anonymous' spec). Wording retained; grounding not possible against provided specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — Passenger Web Portal anonymous sign-on (seven-day journey window) is not in any provided governing spec. Ask the engineer which FBD governs the Passenger Web Portal, then reground.

cases.title: Passenger Portal — sign-on prevented for invalid, no-journey or blocked cards
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that Passenger Web Portal sign-on is prevented for invalid details, a card with no recent journeys, or a blocked card.
preconds: GIVEN the Passenger Web Portal sign-on page is displayed

steps.when: the customer enters invalid details
then: the customer is prevented from signing on
the relevant message is shown

steps.when: the customer enters a card with no journeys in the previous seven days
then: the customer is prevented from signing on
the relevant message is shown

steps.when: the customer enters a blocked card
then: the customer is prevented from signing on
the relevant message is shown

cases.change_note: Split the three failure conditions into three ordered When/Then steps (original bundled them). Behaviour and messages not verifiable against provided specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — no Passenger Web Portal spec provided; the exact rejection messages for each case are unknown. Confirm before running.

cases.title: Passenger Portal — home screen shows balance and summary
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a signed-on customer sees their account balance and a summary of card, account ID and journey/transaction history.
preconds: GIVEN a customer is signed on and the account home screen is displayed
AND the card has completed ABT taps that day

steps.when: the customer views the home screen
then: the account balance is shown
the card details, account ID and journey/transaction history summary is shown

cases.change_note: Wording retained. Not grounded against provided specs (Passenger Web Portal).
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — Passenger Web Portal home-screen contents not in any provided governing spec.

cases.title: Passenger Portal — customer can sign off

cases.title: Settings — each Settings option opens its page
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a CloudFare user with the System Configuration claim can open each option on the Settings menu.
preconds: GIVEN a user is signed into CloudFare with the Dashboard displayed
AND the user holds the System Configuration claim

steps.when: the user opens the Settings menu and selects each listed option in turn
then: each selected option opens its Settings page

cases.change_note: Access to System Configuration is a named CloudFare claim (para 198). This is a navigation smell — selecting 'each option' is not one behaviour. Recommend per-page functional cases (see 4102966-4102972) instead of a single sweep.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — the exact list of Settings menu options is not enumerated in FBD-100342; confirm the live menu contents before finalising this case.

cases.title: Settings — Event Codes view/add/edit/import
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can view, add, edit and import event codes in Settings.
preconds: GIVEN a user is signed into CloudFare on the Event Codes page (holding the System Configuration claim)

steps.when: the user selects an event code and edits it
then: the event codes table reflects the edit

steps.when: the user adds a new event code
then: the new event code appears in the table

steps.when: the user imports event codes
then: the imported codes appear in the table

cases.change_note: Split three actions into ordered steps. Access grounded to the System Configuration claim (para 198); the Event Codes page and its fields are not described in any provided governing spec.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — the Event Codes page and import format are not in the provided governing specs. Confirm which FBD governs CloudFare System Configuration.

steps.when: the user edits an operating unit

steps.when: the user enables or disables the purge for successful quarantine messages

steps.when: the user enables or disables the purge for events and alerts
then: the purge schedule for events and alerts is updated

steps.when: the user enables or disables the purge for communications data
then: the purge schedule for communications data is updated

cases.title: Admin — set End of Operational Day and Week
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an administrator can set the End of the Operational Day and Week that define the capping periods.
preconds: GIVEN an administrator is signed into the ABT Operator Portal with the AdminFullAccess claim
AND the Admin tab is available

steps.when: the administrator sets the End of the Operational Day
then: each operational day is a 24-hour period anchored to that time

steps.when: the administrator sets the End of the Operational Week
then: the operational week is anchored to the configured day

cases.change_note: Split day and week into separate steps. Admin access is grounded to the AdminFullAccess/AdminReadAccess claims (para 146-147); the operational-day/week semantics belong to a capping spec not in the named grounding set.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — the 24-hour operational-day / operational-week definitions are not in the provided governing specs (capping spec not supplied). Confirm the governing FBD.

cases.title: Admin — set the maximum late data period
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an administrator can set the maximum late data period used to process late tap data.
preconds: GIVEN an administrator is signed into the ABT Operator Portal with the AdminFullAccess claim

steps.when: the administrator sets the maximum late data period
then: late tap data is processed according to that period

cases.change_note: Admin access grounded (para 146). Late-data-period semantics not in provided governing specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — maximum late data period behaviour not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Admin — set the maximum journey duration
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an administrator can set the maximum journey duration used to determine an incomplete journey.
preconds: GIVEN an administrator is signed into the ABT Operator Portal with the AdminFullAccess claim

steps.when: the administrator sets the maximum journey duration
then: the duration is used to determine when a journey is treated as incomplete

cases.change_note: Regrounded precondition from 'wants to configure' (not a state) to a proper signed-in admin state. Admin access grounded (para 146). Journey-duration semantics not in provided specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — maximum journey duration behaviour not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Admin — set debt-recovery retry attempts and message
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an administrator can set the online and tap-initiated debt-recovery retry attempts and the unsuccessful-recovery message.
preconds: GIVEN an administrator is signed into the ABT Operator Portal with the AdminFullAccess claim
AND a customer's card is on the deny list

steps.when: the administrator sets the maximum online and tap-initiated retry attempts
then: the customer is limited to that number of retries

steps.when: the administrator sets the unsuccessful-recovery message
then: the configured message is shown on an unsuccessful recovery

cases.change_note: Split retry-limit and message into separate steps. Debt Recovery is a named ABT claim (para 140) and Admin access is grounded (para 146); the retry/message behaviour belongs to a debt-recovery spec not in the named grounding set.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — debt-recovery retry-count and message behaviour not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Admin — set a minimum fare for an e-Purse smartcard
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an administrator can configure a minimum fare for a customer e-Purse smartcard.
preconds: GIVEN an administrator is signed into the ABT Operator Portal with the AdminFullAccess claim (which includes e-Purse access)
AND the Admin tab is displayed

steps.when: the administrator sets a minimum fare for an e-Purse smartcard
then: the minimum fare is saved
the minimum fare is applied to e-Purse validation

cases.change_note: Admin/e-Purse access grounded to AdminFullAccess and the EPurseReadAccess claim (para 146, 148). Minimum-fare-configuration behaviour not in provided governing specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — e-Purse minimum-fare configuration behaviour not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Staff Manager — add a staff member

preconds: GIVEN a user holds the Staff Manager claim
AND the Staff Manager page is displayed with a list of existing staff

steps.when: the user adds a new staff member
then: the new staff record is saved and appears in the list

cases.change_note: Split 'add, modify and disable' into distinct behaviours (recommend companion cases for modify and disable). Staff Manager is a named CloudFare claim (para 185); the add/modify/disable field-level behaviour is not detailed in any provided governing spec.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — the Staff Manager add-staff fields and validation are not described in the provided governing specs (only the claim exists, para 185). Ask which FBD specifies Staff Manager functionality.

preconds: GIVEN a user holds the Staff Manager claim
AND the Staff Manager page shows an existing staff member

steps.when: the user modifies the staff member's PIN
then: the new PIN is saved against the staff record

cases.change_note: Access grounded to the Staff Manager claim (para 185). PIN-modification behaviour not in provided specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — Staff Manager PIN behaviour not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Staff Manager — modify home and working location
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user with the Staff Manager claim can modify a staff member's home and working locations.
preconds: GIVEN a user holds the Staff Manager claim
AND the Staff Manager page shows an existing staff member

steps.when: the user modifies the staff member's home location
then: the updated home location is saved against the staff record

steps.when: the user modifies the staff member's working location
then: the updated working location is saved against the staff record

cases.change_note: Split home/working into two steps. Access grounded (para 185); behaviour not in provided specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — Staff Manager location fields not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Staff Manager — view staff history
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user with the Staff Manager claim can view a staff member's history.
preconds: GIVEN a user holds the Staff Manager claim and the Staff Manager module is available

steps.when: the user views a staff member's history
then: the staff history is displayed

cases.change_note: Access grounded (para 185). Staff history contents not in provided specs.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — Staff Manager history contents not in provided governing specs.

cases.title: Ticket Editor — create a ticket template
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can create a new ticket template in the Ticket Editor.
preconds: GIVEN a user is signed into CloudFare and holds the Ticket Editor claim (access to the Tickets sub-module)
AND the Ticket Editor is open at the main entry screen showing existing templates and the Create / Edit / Copy options

steps.when: the user presses Create, enters a template name and selects a device type, then confirms
then: a blank ticket template preview is displayed, bounded by the device's default paper dimensions and orientation

cases.change_note: Split 'create, edit and copy' into three cases — the spec presents Create / Edit / Copy as three distinct entry options (para 254-257). Regrounded 'layout' to 'template' (the spec's term throughout). Create requires a template name and device type at creation (para 180). Access is the Ticket Editor claim (FBD-100342 para 177). Companion cases: Edit an existing template (para 256, 290-328) and Copy an existing template (para 257, 329-352).

cases.title: Ticket Editor — add elements to a template
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can add the Ticket Editor elements (fixed text, dynamic field, logo/image, line separator, barcode) to a ticket template.
preconds: GIVEN a ticket template is loaded in the Ticket Editor preview

steps.when: the user adds a fixed text element and a dynamic field element
then: the fixed text is placed on the preview
the dynamic field name is shown in green on the preview

steps.when: the user adds a logo/image and a line separator
then: the logo is shown on the preview
the separator line is shown on the preview

cases.change_note: Named the real element types from the left-hand element menu (para 362-366): Fixed Text, Dynamic Field, Logo/Image, Line Separator, Barcode. Dynamic fields display in green on the preview (para 191). Barcode has its own case (4103086).

cases.title: Ticket Editor — copy a template and change its device type
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can reuse a ticket template on another device type by copying it and changing the device type (each device type has its own template).
preconds: GIVEN a ticket template exists for one device type (e.g. an ETM template)
AND the Ticket Editor is open at the main entry screen

steps.when: the user copies the template and changes the device type on the copy (e.g. ETM to POS)
then: a separate template is created for the new device type

cases.change_note: Regrounded: a single ticket 'layout' is NOT configured across multiple devices. Device type is fixed at creation and separate templates are required per device type (para 178-180); the supported flow is to copy a template and change the device type (para 338). Retitled and rescoped accordingly.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — device-type change is cautioned where fonts/paper width differ (para 338); the tester should verify the copy renders correctly on the new device before relying on it.

cases.title: Ticket Editor — configure a change ticket (NOT IN SPEC)
cases.preface: This test is to confirm configuration of a 'change ticket'. NOTE: no 'change ticket' concept is described in the Ticket Editor spec.
preconds: GIVEN a user is in the Ticket Editor

steps.when: the user attempts to configure a change ticket
then: **GAP** — a 'change ticket' is not defined in FBD-100363

cases.change_note: FBD-100363 describes paper tickets, smartcard receipts, barcode validation tickets and payment card receipts (para 125, 155-159). There is NO 'change ticket' type or configuration in the spec.
gaps: **GAP** — 'change ticket' is not in FBD-100363. Clarify with the engineer what a 'change ticket' means (a money-change receipt? a ticket-amendment flow?) and which spec/CR governs it before retaining this case.

cases.title: Product Editor — assign a ticket template to a product
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a published ticket template can be assigned to a ticket type or product class in the Product Editor.
preconds: GIVEN a ticket template has been published from the Ticket Editor (making it available in the Product Editor)
AND a user is in the Product Editor on the product configuration tab

steps.when: the user selects a ticket template for the product/ticket type from the drop-down of available templates
then: the ticket template is assigned to the product

cases.change_note: Cross-surface correction: assigning a template to a product/ticket type is a PRODUCT EDITOR function, not a Ticket Editor function (para 391-393). The Ticket Editor only creates and publishes templates (para 250). Retitled and moved the action to the Product Editor. Recommend re-filing this case under Products.

cases.title: Ticket Editor — group a set of ticket layouts (NOT IN SPEC)
cases.preface: This test is to confirm grouping of ticket layouts. NOTE: no ticket-layout grouping feature is described in the Ticket Editor spec.
preconds: GIVEN a user is in the Ticket Editor with ticket templates available

steps.when: the user attempts to group a set of ticket templates
then: **GAP** — no ticket-template grouping feature exists in FBD-100363

cases.change_note: FBD-100363 exposes only Create/Edit/Copy on templates (para 254) and per-level publishing; templates relate to products via the Product Editor (para 391). There is no 'group a set of ticket layouts' feature. The nearest real concepts are the CloudFare hierarchy level a template is published at, and product classes — neither is 'grouping layouts'.
gaps: **GAP** — 'group a set of ticket layouts' is not in FBD-100363. Confirm whether this means publishing at a hierarchy level, product-class association, or a feature that does not exist.

cases.title: Ticket Editor — add a barcode to a template
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can add a barcode element to a ticket template using the barcode tool.
preconds: GIVEN a user has a ticket template open in the Ticket Editor and holds the Ticket Editor claim

steps.when: the user selects the barcode tool and places a barcode at the end of the ticket
then: a size-accurate representative barcode image is shown on the preview at the placed position

cases.change_note: Grounded barcode placement (para 260-263, 383-385). The preview barcode is illustrative/size-accurate only — the device generates the real barcode (para 262, 264). Spec advises placing the barcode at the very end of the ticket (para 263).

cases.title: Ticket Editor — add payment-card fields to a template
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can add the payment-card fields to a ticket template: unique reference number, obfuscated card number, printed serial number, card start date and expiry date.
preconds: GIVEN a user has a payment-card receipt template open in the Ticket Editor and holds the Ticket Editor claim

steps.when: the user adds the payment-card dynamic/optional fields to the template
then: the obfuscated Payment Card Number field is added (REQ-1750.20)
the Payment Card Unique Reference Number field is added (REQ-1750.21)
the Printed Serial Number field is added (REQ-1750.18)

steps.when: the user adds the card date fields
then: the Card Start Date field is added (REQ-1750.17)
the Expiry Date field is added (REQ-1750.16)

cases.change_note: Each field maps to a requirement: obfuscated PAN REQ-1750.20 (para 141), unique ref REQ-1750.21 (para 142), Printed Serial Number REQ-1750.18 (para 139), card start date REQ-1750.17 (para 138), expiry REQ-1750.16 (para 137). Split into two steps to keep <=3 predicates per THEN. Note: these are added as dynamic/optional fields; payment-card receipt changes are cosmetic only per EMV (para 159).

cases.title: Drawing Tool — add a new map point with a linked stop
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can add a new map point, including a linked stop, with the Drawing Tool.
preconds: GIVEN a user holds the Topology claim and is on the Topology & Fares Management Drawing Tool

then: the map point is created

cases.change_note: Access grounded to the Topology claim (access to Topology & Fares module, para 174). The Drawing Tool's map-point/stop functions are not described in any provided governing spec.
gaps: **UNCONFIRMED** — Drawing Tool map-point/linked-stop behaviour not in provided governing specs. Ask which FBD governs the Topology & Fares Drawing Tool.

cases.title: Drawing Tool — create, edit and delete a zone
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can create, edit and delete a zone, with a smaller zone layered above a larger overlaid zone so it stays accessible.
preconds: GIVEN a user holds the Topology claim and is on the Topology & Fares Management Drawing Tool

steps.when: the user creates a zone
then: the zone is created on the map

steps.when: the user edits the zone
then: the edit is applied to the zone

steps.when: the user deletes the zone
